By Javier Molero/ jmolero@eurohoops.net   
Pierria Henry will undergo a trial period with Maccabi Tel Aviv. As initially reported by Chema de Lucas and Israeli journalist Moses Barda, the point guard—who has previously played for teams including Baskonia and Fenerbahçe—is returning to the EuroLeague with the Israeli club after nearly four years away.
Maccabi has issued a statement on its social media channels confirming the news:
Even before the injury to Ife Lundberg, Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv had reached an agreement to bring in point guard Pierria Henry for a trial period. Henry (33)—who will be eligible to return to competitive play in January 2027—was signed in September, and a decision on whether to add him to the club permanently will be made during this training period. Regardless of his arrival, Maccabi plans to finalize the signing of another player in the coming days.
Pierria Henry (1.93m, 33 years old) is an American point guard who also holds Senegalese citizenship and possesses extensive EuroLeague experience. He played for Fenerbahçe and spent three seasons with Baskonia. Earlier in his career, he played in Germany, Turkey, and Russia, and also had a stint in Israel, where he played for Hapoel Eilat (2016/17). In his most recent EuroLeague season, he averaged 9.9 points.
The last game Henry played was for the Vitoria-based club in January 2023. That same month, Baskonia suspended his contract. He was sanctioned for the use—or attempted use—of a prohibited method (tampering with a urine sample/evidence of synthetic urine) during an anti-doping test conducted following a EuroLeague match between Baskonia and Maccabi Tel Aviv on November 3, 2022.
FIBA officially imposed a four-year (48-month) ban in February 2024, which is set to expire in January 2027—meaning Henry could be eligible to play in the coming weeks. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) rejected his appeal in 2025, upholding the sanction, which is now nearing its end.
In an unexpected turn of events, Henry could land at Maccabi Tel Aviv, a team currently sitting in second-to-last place in the EuroLeague standings with a record of 2 wins and 8 losses. The 33-year-old American-Senegalese point guard appears ready to return to the highest level of European basketball.
